features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows real experience shipping AI features in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure handling.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is stated.
AI is mentioned vaguely or aspirationally, without shipped work.
The letter states that AI or LLM-backed features were built and shipped in production.
The letter shows shipped AI systems plus reliability work such as evaluation, hardening, trustworthiness, or handling failure modes.

features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment the letter cites as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on design of agent-based systems, especially bounded autonomy, orchestration, and supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering problem-solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and readiness to partner closely with security specialists and internal users.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal collaboration with security specialists or users of the tooling.
Uses general teamwork or internal-customer language, but without much specificity.
Explicitly wants to work closely with security engineers, learn from domain specialists, or build in tight proximity to the teams served.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through safe defaults, usable tooling, reduced friction, and internal-customer empathy.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter supports claims with named systems, mechanisms, accomplishments, outcomes, or impact rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go backend depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central production language for backend systems.

levels.descriptor: Go is missing, unclear, or only incidental.
Go is mentioned as a language used, but not as a main vehicle for work.
Go is clearly presented as the primary or day-to-day language.
Go is central to multiple production systems or explicitly tied to backend or security-infrastructure ownership.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on maintainability, reliability, engineering rigor, and long-term operational care rather than only shipping features.

levels.descriptor: No maintainer or operational mindset is visible.
Mentions maintenance or testing as duties but does not turn that into a design perspective.
Explicitly frames the applicant as a maintainer who values durability, inheritance, or real-world failure modes.
Uses maintenance or failure experience to explain a clear philosophy for how secure systems should be designed and operated.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter reads as a coherent, well-structured story or argument with a clear arc rather than a disconnected list of claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative voice
features.description: Captures whether the letter has a memorable, distinctive, and individual voice or framing rather than sounding templated.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial skill-building, especially through CTFs or similar attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary development work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution to, maintenance of, or responsibility for software and fixes used beyond the applicant's immediate employer or team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: Captures how much independent responsibility, authorship, or system ownership the letter claims over the work it describes.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how technically ambitious, sustained, and revealing the applicant's self-directed projects or side work appear.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
The project mentioned is small and mainly serves as lightweight practice or curiosity.
The project shows substantial self-directed engineering with meaningful system design or operational concerns.
The project is an ambitious systems build that tackles hard distributed-systems, storage, or reliability problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or systems.

levels.descriptor: No real signal of interest in shared infrastructure or broad downstream impact.
General statements about scale or impact without tying them to platform work.
Explicitly says they prefer foundational or internal tooling work with organization-wide reach.
Frames past choices and future goals around compounding leverage from shared systems across many teams.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth and breadth of real production software experience conveyed through years of work, shipped systems, lifecycle ownership, and operational responsibility.

levels.descriptor: Meets the minimum bar only, with limited production history or few concrete examples of launched services.
Shows a solid early-career production record, with some launch and maintenance experience but modest cumulative depth.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with repeated launch and maintenance ownership across multiple production services.
Shows extensive production depth, combining long tenure with repeated delivery and operation of many production services.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, automation, or tooling.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter targets this exact role by explaining why it fits the applicant and by mapping prior experience onto the posting's requirements.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems for security issues through activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, and remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role's core problem as scaling security work through principled automation, workflow design, and security-at-scale thinking.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: Captures the strength of formal third-party security certifications or other external credential signals cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Security philosophy and commitment
features.description: Captures whether the letter conveys a substantive security-engineering point of view, identity, or authentic commitment to security work itself.

levels.descriptor: Reads as a general software engineer with little security grounding.
Reads as security-adjacent and interested in learning more.
Shows established security practice through multiple direct activities.
Conveys a mature security-engineering identity, with a clear attacker, builder, or rigor-first philosophy.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building systems that automate intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface-level mechanical quality of the prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures whether the letter includes third-party validation of security skills and how demanding that validation is.

levels.descriptor: No external security credential is mentioned.
A fundamentals-oriented credential such as Security+ is presented.
A more hands-on, advanced credential such as OSCP is presented.
